test_policy.notes: Test scores are not required for admission. Admission needs a high school GPA of at least 2.00; a GPA of 3.00+ (or 2.00+ with ACT 19 / SAT 990) is admitted directly to the major's college, and test-free applicants with a 2.00-2.99 GPA enter University College. International applicants may need official SAT/ACT for direct entry to some programs (e.g. Science, Engineering and Computer Sciences, Nursing). Scores are also used for scholarships.

requirements.notes: International degree-seeking application fees are currently waived (the Common Data Set also lists $0). Required: official secondary coursework sent from the issuing school (a NACES/AICE evaluation is an optional alternative), minimum 2.00 GPA (converted by the International Admissions Office), proof of English proficiency, and ACT/SAT for some majors. The Common Data Set's admission-factor checkboxes were unreadable, so the essay and recommendation policy is not shown.

deadlines.label: International fall application deadline (fall 2027 entry)
deadlines.notes: All required documents must be received by the Fall June 15 date to guarantee consideration (Spring Oct. 15, Summer Mar. 15). The page prints no year; fall 2027 assumed. The CDS lists a domestic priority/closing date of 8/23 and rolling notification from Sept. 1.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Exempt: equivalent of a U.S. high school diploma or college degree from an approved English-speaking country (list on the page); one year of study at a U.S. high school with a C or higher in English; 24 undergraduate credits at a U.S.-accredited university; transfer credit equivalent to ENG 101 with C or better; completion of an approved ESL program; IGCSE/O-Level English First Language C or higher; IB English A (HL 4+, SL 5+). SAT EBRW 480 or ACT English/Reading 18 also satisfy the requirement. Marshall's pages do not describe a conditional admission pathway.

english.notes: Exams taken after 2026-01-20: the page lists '4.0 or 72' for undergraduates (4.5 or 86 for graduate). The 1-6 band is assumed from the 4.0/4.5 values.
PTE Academic or PTE Express. The undergraduate catalog lists PTEA 50, which conflicts with the international admissions page (57); 57 is the international page value.

aid.notes: International students count as nonresidents for scholarships. The John Marshall Scholarship (freshman merit; high school GPA and, where applicable, test scores) pays nonresidents $14,000 (GPA 3.9+ with ACT 30/SAT 1360), $9,000 (GPA 3.8), $7,000 (GPA 3.5) or $5,000 (GPA 3.0) per year; it is renewable for four years. Only the college's own non-need-based aid is available to nonresidents (Common Data Set).
